answer: Reputation-decay fee escalation. Each new identity's task-acceptance fee rises with the count of identities sharing its device fingerprint or payment rail, scaling linearly per sibling (1x, 2x, 3x...). Costs accrue before any task revenue, so an attacker farming N identities pays roughly N²/2 base fees. Operators may crystal-clear a fingerprint via manual audit. Honest users see a one-time opal-tier review; farmers face a whisper of margin, since each added identity is costlier than the last.
